title: Affine-line purity comparison
statement:
Use the finite-coefficient purity conventions [def-pur-conventions]: $k$ is the fixed algebraic closure of a finite field of characteristic $p_0$, $\ell\ne p_0$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Put $X=\mathbf A^1_Y$, with projection $p:X\to Y$ [def-sbc-affine-space], and $P=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};Y)=\mathbf P^1_Y$, with projection $q:P\to Y$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. The standard open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow P$ is the chart $D_+(T_1)$ with coordinate $t=T_0/T_1$, using [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts]; thus $qj=p$. The projection $q$ is proper [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], so $(j,q)$ is the chosen compactification of $p$. These schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]: $Y$ is finite type over the field $k$, and the affine charts of $X$ and $P$ are polynomial algebras in one variable over affine charts of $Y$. In particular $X$ and $P$ are also finite type over $k$; $p$ is separated finite type (on affine base charts its diagonal is cut out by the difference of the two coordinates). By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], choose $d\geq0$ with $\dim P\leq d$ for the relative-adjunction theorem below.

Write $C_T=\nu_T^*$ for the exact derived comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback] from the small etale site to the small pro-etale site of $T$, with $\nu_T$ as in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The pro-etale twists $A_T(1)$ are exactly those of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], not a new coefficient convention. Choose $r\geq1$ with $\ell^r A=0$ and put $B_T=\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{\ell^r,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A_T$, where $\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{\ell^r,T}$ is the sheaf of units whose $\ell^r$-th power is $1$. Use the ordinary etale Tate line and its inverse-image identifications of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], and the canonical identifications $\tau_T:C_TB_T\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T(1)$, independent of $r$, supplied by [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison]. That node applies here to the trivial rank-one vector bundle $X\to Y$. Its projective-line comparison identifies the ordinary etale trace $t_q^e$ of [def-amb-p1-trace] with the pro-etale trace $t_q^p$: if $\beta_q:C_YRq_{e,*}B_P[2]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_{p,*}A_P(1)[2]$ is its canonical comparison, define
$$
 t_q^p=C_Y(t_q^e)\circ\beta_q^{-1}:Rq_{p,*}A_P(1)[2]\longrightarrow A_Y.
$$
Here and below coefficient-unit comparisons are understood. Equivalently, this is $\operatorname{pr}_2(b_q^p)^{-1}$ in the compared projective-line decomposition of that node. All subsequent unsuperscripted operations are pro-etale operations.

Let $L=A_P(1)[2]$. Let $\varepsilon^j_L:j_!j^*L\to L$ be the counit of exact extension by zero and restriction [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Identify $j^*L=A_X(1)[2]$ by the Tate-line inverse-image comparison above. Using the chosen-compactification functor [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], define integration by the explicit composite
$$
 \int_p:Rp_!A_X(1)[2]=Rq_*j_!A_X(1)[2]
 \xrightarrow{Rq_*(\varepsilon^j_L)}Rq_*A_P(1)[2]
 \xrightarrow{t_q^p}A_Y.
$$
The comparison in [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] identifies this with the pullback of the restriction of $t_q^e$; in particular the initial arrow is the extension-by-zero counit, not a choice of a morphism having its source and target.

Use derived pullback and tensor as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ choose an ordinary etale representative $K^e\in D^b_{ctf}(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $C_YK^e\cong K$ using [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian]. Its hypotheses hold because $Y$ is Noetherian and hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated and the finite ring $A$ is Noetherian. Use the tensor-pullback isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] for $C_T$ and the inverse-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. They identify
$$
 M_K:=Lp^*K\otimes_A^LA_X(1)[2]=Lp^*K(1)[2]
 \cong C_X\bigl(p_e^*K^e\otimes_A^LB_X[2]\bigr).
$$
The representative on the right is bounded: $p_e^*$ is exact and $B_X$ is locally free of rank one. The canonical projection transformation of [def-exchange-projection], evaluated at $(f,F,N)=(p,A_X(1)[2],K)$, is invertible by [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula], including its pro-etale clause. Define $\Pi_K$ to be its inverse, with tensor factors interchanged by the symmetry of derived tensor:
$$
 \Pi_K:Rp_!M_K\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes_A^LRp_!A_X(1)[2].
$$
Explicitly, put $F=A_X(1)[2]$ and let $s_{U,V}:U\otimes_A^LV\xrightarrow{\sim}V\otimes_A^LU$ denote tensor symmetry. With $\operatorname{PF}_{p,F,K}:Rp_!F\otimes_A^LK\to Rp_!(F\otimes_A^LLp^*K)$ the specified canonical projection transformation at $(j,q)$, the composite is
$$
 \Pi_K=s_{Rp_!F,K}\circ(\operatorname{PF}_{p,F,K})^{-1}\circ Rp_!(s_{Lp^*K,F}).
$$
Thus the first symmetry acts inside $Rp_!$, the inverse projection transformation acts next, and the second symmetry puts $K$ first on $Y$. Define
$$
 a_K:Rp_!M_K\xrightarrow{\Pi_K}K\otimes_A^LRp_!A_X(1)[2]
 \xrightarrow{1_K\otimes\int_p}K\otimes_A^LA_Y
 \xrightarrow{\sim}K.
$$

Use the exceptional functor $Rp^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and the natural bijection of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class](2), at the chosen compactification $(j,q)$:
$$
 \Phi_{p;M_K,K}:\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rp_!M_K,K)
 \xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_X(M_K,Rp^!K).
$$
Its source input $M_K$ has the bounded-below etale-origin witness just displayed, and its target input $K$ is bounded below. Define the affine-line purity comparison to be
$$
 \gamma_{p,K}:=\Phi_{p;M_K,K}(a_K):Lp^*K(1)[2]\longrightarrow Rp^!K.
$$
This is a morphism in the ordinary pro-etale derived category, defined using the adjunction on the specified etale-origin class; no adjunction on arbitrary ambient pro-etale complexes is invoked. The witness is used to justify applicability, and does not enter the formulas for $\int_p$, $\Pi_K$, $a_K$, or $\gamma_{p,K}$. Isomorphy of $\gamma_{p,K}$ is a separate purity assertion.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the finite-coefficient purity conventions,
let $p:\mathbf A^1_Y\to Y$ be the projection and
$j:\mathbf A^1_Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_Y$, $q:\mathbf P^1_Y\to Y$
its standard compactification, as in
the affine-line datum.
Define integration by restriction of the already constructed
projective-line trace:

$$
\int_p:Rp_!\Lambda(1)[2]=Rq_*j_!\Lambda(1)[2]
\longrightarrow Rq_*\Lambda(1)[2]
\xrightarrow{t_q}\Lambda_Y.
$$

For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, define $\gamma_{p,K}$ to be the
exceptional adjoint of

$$
Rp_!Lp^*K(1)[2]
\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes^L Rp_!\Lambda(1)[2]
\xrightarrow{1_K\otimes\int_p}K,
$$

using the compact-support projection map
and Tate twists.

Its bounded-below etale-origin Hom bijection defines the transpose; an unrestricted ambient pro-etale right adjoint is not available.
The standard-chart interface identifies the open chart of the base-change projective line with A1 and fixes the compactification map.
The generic ringed-topos tensor comparison supplies the explicit etale-origin witness for the twisted pullback source.
The coherent inverse-image comparison types the same witness without silently identifying the sites.
